wasmLinkerPort.status: Experimental Tower static Wasm linker supports edited browser self-builds, lazy archives and nonshared imported memory. Measured repeated hashing, UTF-8 and relocation work removed in Tower. Production LLD dispatch retained.
wasmLinkerPort.validation: Fresh public-bootstrap native successor/backend API and expanded native/WASI fixtures pass. Hash collisions, Unicode boundaries, padded LEB validation and unordered relocation ownership checked. Whole/lazy LLVM images are byte-identical to baseline; 12 selected interpreter/raw/optimized checks pass. Optimized Tower linker inside Wasm passes two edited portable/LLVM/cross self-build generations with identical successor hashes across two/four compilation workers.
wasmLinkerPort.remaining: Shared-memory atomic initialization, TLS and concurrent instantiation; actual parallel linker parsing/relocation jobs with deterministic joins; debug/profile coverage and production cutover. Native ELF/COFF/Mach-O remain later work.
wasmLinkerPort.availability: Source/API performance validation receipt only; hosted runtime assets/build-source identity are preserved, with default LLD dispatch unchanged.
wasmLinkerPort.benchmark: Frozen LLVM-reactor inputs, five uninstrumented paired runs: previous Tower median 0.53 s; optimized Tower 0.42 s; SDK34 LLD 0.44 s. About 21% faster than previous Tower and 5% faster than LLD on this workload, with identical output. Callgrind executed instructions fall 27.1%, 3.173B to 2.315B. Cached indexes add about 6 MiB; optimized RSS about 343 MiB versus LLD 368 MiB. No universal platform/workload speed claim.
